cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Accurate written description requires precise dance terminology, not everyday language

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Movement description should cover action, dynamics, space and relationships (A D S R)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Action vocabulary includes actions of the body: turn, jump, travel, gesture, fall, stillness

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Dynamics describe how movements are performed: fast, slow, sustained, sudden, heavy, light

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Spatial description includes levels, directions, pathways, formations and use of stage space

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Relationships describe how dancers interact: unison, canon, contact, complement, contrast

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Always describe what you see in specific, concrete terms rather than vague impressions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Avoid subjective language like 'beautiful' or 'amazing' — use technical observations instead

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Use the present tense when describing what happens in a dance: 'the dancer leaps', not 'leapt'

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Reference specific moments, counts or sections to show detailed knowledge of the work

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Link descriptive points to the choreographic intention for higher-mark questions

cards.front: Recall a key point about Describing Dance in Writing
cards.back: Practise writing movement descriptions from memory to build fluency with terminology

cards.front: What should you know about gcse dance exam tips — describing dance in writing?
cards.back: 1. For Describing Dance in Writing questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Describing Dance in Writing 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
Describe the movement in a section of a professional dance work you have studied, using accurate dance terminology. [6 marks]

AO1 (Performance): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of describing dance in writing, including choreographic processes, performing skills and dance appreciation relevant to AQA 8236. AO2 (Choreography): Apply knowledge and understanding of describing dance in writing through the creative process of choreography, selecting and using movement material and choreographic devices.
